newsitem.title: UK: UK could suffer outside EMU - Labour's Cook.
newsitem.headline: UK could suffer outside EMU - Labour's Cook.

text.p: Britain would suffer penalties if it did not join a successful European monetary union, the foreign affairs spokesman of the opposition Labour Party, Robin Cook, said on Monday.
"In the longer term, there would be penalities from staying outside (a single currency)," Cook told BBC radio in an interview.
Cook repeated Labour's view that in the immediate future, Britain could only join a single currency if it achieved real economic convergence with other participating countries.

"If not, there may well be difficulties for us being within a single currency prematurely," he said. "In the longer run though...a country that stays out of the European single currency could face penalties.
"For instance inward investment decisions taken in Tokyo, taken in Dallas, are more likely to go within the single core currency than into an offshore currency."
"Moreover we would have the full weight of international currency speculation coming on the pound because it was the one outside."

Cook said any Conservative politicians who said Britain should stay out of a single currency even if it went ahead and proved successful were "making a very major statement about the extent to which they are prepared to damage Britain's economic interests because of their own dogmatic stance on Europe."
